note:
The deck suite, scored on PPTAgent's PPTEval dimensions: Content, Design and Coherence.

The mechanical half of each dimension is asserted here. Content is slide count, bullet length, filler and placeholder copy, and whether metrics carry a real number. Design is layout variety and, most importantly, whether any slide's text runs off the bottom - measured in a browser, because it is invisible in the JSON and fatal on a projector. Coherence is the deck opening on a title and closing on what happens next.

What is not asserted is whether the argument is any good. That is the part of PPTEval a rubric and a human do, and pretending a script can is how an eval suite stops meaning anything.

tasks.prompt: Build a short deck for a meeting with a mortgage broker who might refer clients to us. Ten minutes, one person in the room.
Build a deck for a meeting with an estate manager deciding whether to put hedgerow work out to a specialist. We want them to book a walk along the hedge.
Build a deck for a cafe owner we want to supply. Five minutes over a coffee. They care about consistency and delivery time.
Build a deck introducing the practice for a local estate agents' team meeting, so their negotiators know when to recommend us.
